facts.fact: Guinea's president signed a decree on 19 August 2026 applying article 1003 of the Civil Code on electronic signature, giving an electronic signature the same probative force as a paper writing, covering public, private and person-to-person acts, and taking effect on signature.
facts.system: Decree applying article 1003 of the Civil Code on electronic signature

facts.fact: The decree of 19 August 2026 requires every electronic-certification service provider to be approved by the competent authority, names the national digital agency ANDE as that authority for approval, control and audit, and refers technical standards to a joint order of the telecommunications and justice ministries; it reports no provider approved.
facts.system: Decree applying article 1003 of the Civil Code on electronic signature

facts.fact: Law L/2016/035/AN of 26 July 2016 on electronic transactions was promulgated; ANSSI's summary says it applies to all electronic transactions including online commerce, and covers electronic signature, digital archiving, system certification, consumer information duties, fines and prison terms (the document is a summary of an image-only scan).
facts.system: Loi L/2016/035/AN relative aux transactions electroniques

note: Reports a Guinean delegation comparing procurement platforms (APPEL, TELEMO); it states nothing about an electronic transactions or e-commerce law.

systems.system: Décret on security audit, control and certification of information systems used in electronic transactions (read on national television 21 May 2026)
systems.tiers: all public and private enterprises and establishments in electronic transactions, and foreign firms serving Guinean residents

note: The decree reported is a cybersecurity audit and certification regime run by ARPT; the article does not say it is made under an electronic transactions or e-commerce law, so it is class other and gives no fact.

facts.fact: ANSSI's page states that Decree D/2021/092/PRG/SGG, signed 25 March 2021 under Law L/2016/035/AN of 26 July 2016 on electronic transactions, sets rules for electronic transactions including e-commerce (secure transaction facility, .gn or .com domain, prices in francs), names the ARPT as regulator with sanction powers, and provides fines and penalties (the scan itself is image-only, so this is ANSSI's summary).
facts.system: Décret D/2021/092/PRG/SGG portant sur les transactions électroniques

systems.system: Loi L/2016/035/AN relative aux transactions électroniques
Décret D/2021/092/PRG/SGG portant sur les transactions électroniques
systems.tiers: all natural and legal persons, public and private, in electronic transactions

note: Covers consumer protection for inclusive financial institutions; says nothing of electronic transactions or online selling.

facts.fact: A government representative said article 1003 of the Civil Code gives strict equivalence between handwritten and electronic signature, per Guineenews.
Guineenews reports an implementing decree fixing the modalities of electronic signature under article 1003 of the Civil Code was adopted on 19 August 2026.

note: UNCTAD lists Law L/2016/035/AN; already held as GIN-003.

facts.fact: ANDE's director general and the minister cited the 19 August 2026 presidential decree instituting electronic signature, with ANDE as its regulator, alongside Article 1003 of the Civil Code; the decree covers electronic signature only.
facts.system: decree of 19 August 2026 on electronic signature

facts.fact: The minister said the first step, the regulatory framework and the implementing orders of the decree, is now complete; nine draft implementing texts had been examined on 21 October 2026.
facts.system: decree of 19 August 2026 on electronic signature
